evals.expected_output: Discovers the project-owned build, reinstall, and verification commands, shows the plan, builds first, reinstalls only the proven output, and verifies the installed copy against it.
assertions: Build, reinstall, and verification commands come from the project rather than being guessed from a framework name.
The plan is displayed before the installed target is changed.
The reinstall runs only after the build exits zero.
The installed copy is verified against the build rather than assumed correct.

evals.prompt: Rebuild and reinstall the CLI. The build fails on a type error partway through.
evals.expected_output: Stops on the first non-zero exit, reports the failing command and its output, and leaves the installed target untouched.
assertions: The workflow stops at the first failing command.
The previously installed target is not modified after a failed build.
The failing command and its output are reported instead of a summary judgement.

evals.prompt: You just finished the refactor — go ahead and reinstall so I can try it.
evals.expected_output: Confirms that this is an explicit request before running, and never treats finishing other work as its own trigger.
assertions: The workflow runs only from an explicit request, not as an automatic post-completion step.
The explicit-request rule is stated when the trigger is ambiguous.
No install-changing command runs before the request is confirmed.

evals.prompt: Reinstall it. The verification command needs a running daemon we do not have here — just report success if the install command exits zero.
evals.expected_output: Reports the install result and the unavailable runtime proof separately, and refuses to call the reinstall verified.
assertions: A zero exit from the install command is not treated as end-to-end proof.
Checks that could not run are reported as unavailable, separately from checks that passed.
The reinstall is labeled unverified rather than successful.
